name: Congo
tagline: Odzala, and the western lowland gorilla
summary: Odzala-Kokoua is one of the best places on earth to track western lowland gorillas, Nouabale-Ndoki has forest that has never been logged, and the Congo river runs the whole eastern border.
when: The two dry seasons: June to August, and December to February.

entries.caption: Odzala-Kokoua
entries.description: Forest, savanna and bais together, and gorillas habituated for tracking on foot.
entries.subject: a forest bai clearing surrounded by rainforest in Odzala

entries.caption: The Congo Basin
entries.description: Two thirds of the country is rainforest, and much of it has never had a road in it.
entries.subject: unbroken Congo Basin rainforest canopy from the air

entries.caption: Western Lowland Gorillas
entries.description: Smaller, redder and harder to see than mountain gorillas, and tracked through swamp forest.
entries.subject: a silverback western lowland gorilla in dense green forest

entries.caption: Bai Watching
entries.description: Forest buffalo, bongo, sitatunga and elephant come to the clearings, and you sit and wait.
entries.subject: forest buffalo and elephants at a bai in Odzala

entries.caption: Mount Berongou
entries.description: 903 metres in the Mayombe, and the highest ground in a country of forest and plateau.
entries.subject: the forested Mayombe hills under low cloud

entries.caption: The Loufoulakari
entries.description: Falls on the Congo above Brazzaville, where the river drops through rock.
entries.subject: the Loufoulakari falls dropping through rock into the Congo

entries.caption: The Congo River
entries.description: The second largest river on earth by volume, and the whole eastern border of the country.
entries.subject: the vast brown Congo river with forest on the far bank

entries.caption: A Hundred and Seventy Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Pointe-Noire's beaches, and the empty sand of the Conkouati coast north of it.
entries.subject: an empty Atlantic beach backed by forest at Conkouati

entries.caption: Nouabale-Ndoki
entries.description: Forest that has never been logged, and the Goualougo Triangle where the chimps had not seen people.
entries.subject: old-growth rainforest with enormous buttressed trees at Ndoki

entries.caption: Forest and River
entries.description: Pirogue on the Lekoli, tracking on foot, and nights on a bai platform.
entries.subject: a pirogue moving up a narrow forest river in Odzala

entries.caption: Congolese Rumba
entries.description: Rumba was made on both banks of this river, and it is on the UNESCO list because of it.
entries.subject: a rumba band performing at a bar in Brazzaville

entries.caption: Kongo, Teke, Mbochi and the Aka
entries.description: Bantu peoples along the river, and Aka forest hunter-gatherers in the north.
entries.subject: an Aka forest camp with leaf shelters in the north

entries.caption: Saka-Saka and Poulet Moambe
entries.description: Cassava leaf, and chicken in palm nut sauce — the dish of both Congos.
entries.subject: a plate of poulet moambe with cassava and rice

entries.caption: The Feux de Brazza
entries.description: A music festival in Brazzaville, and rumba the rest of the year in every bar.
entries.subject: a crowd dancing at a music festival in Brazzaville

entries.caption: Raffia, Masks and Nkisi
entries.description: Raffia weaving, Teke masks, and Kongo nkisi power figures.
entries.subject: a flat round Teke mask with geometric carving

entries.caption: Brazzaville's Colonial Core
entries.description: The Case de Gaulle and the Basilique Sainte-Anne, and a river frontage facing Kinshasa.
entries.subject: the pointed roof of the Basilique Sainte-Anne in Brazzaville

entries.caption: Sangha Trinational
entries.description: Nouabale-Ndoki is part of the World Heritage forest shared with Cameroon and CAR.
entries.subject: old-growth forest and a river in the Sangha Trinational park

entries.caption: Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire
entries.description: A river capital looking across at Kinshasa, and an Atlantic oil port with the beaches.
entries.subject: the Congo river frontage at Brazzaville with Kinshasa opposite

entries.caption: Colonial and Forest
entries.description: French colonial along the river, and the Poto-Poto quarter that gave its name to a painting school.
entries.subject: a colonial-era verandah building in Brazzaville

entries.caption: The Bars of Poto-Poto
entries.description: Rumba, grilled fish and beer, from the afternoon until it is not the afternoon.
entries.subject: an open-air bar with music in the Poto-Poto quarter

entries.caption: Not Really
entries.description: Odzala is a long way in and expensive. This is a trip for adults who want gorillas.
entries.subject: a light aircraft on a grass strip beside forest

entries.caption: Tracking and Pirogue
entries.description: Long days on foot through swamp forest, and quiet mornings on the Lekoli.
entries.subject: trackers wading a shallow forest stream

entries.caption: Small and Excellent
entries.description: Odzala's camps are among the best-run in Central Africa, and there are three of them.
entries.subject: a raised forest camp deck overlooking a bai in Odzala

entries.caption: Odzala's Model
entries.description: Ex-poachers employed as trackers, and revenue shared with the villages on the park edge.
entries.subject: a Congolese tracker pointing out gorilla sign in forest

entries.caption: Green and Steam
entries.description: A bai at first light, when the mist is still on it and the elephants are already there.
entries.subject: mist over a forest bai at dawn with elephants in it

entries.caption: Lesio-Louna
entries.description: A gorilla sanctuary on the Bateke plateau, two hours from Brazzaville.
entries.subject: gorillas on a wooded island in the Lesio-Louna sanctuary

entries.caption: Why Congo
entries.description: The best western lowland gorilla tracking anywhere, in forest that has never been cut.
entries.subject: a gorilla family moving through dense green forest
